sentences.text: This interlocutory application has been preferred by the appellant for grant of bail to him during the pendency of this appeal.

The appellant has been convicted for the offences under Section 6 of the POCSO Act as well as under Sections 323, 341 and 376(2)(n) of I.P.C. and has been sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for 20 years for the offence under Section 6 of the POCSO Act.

It has been alleged that the informant - victim was subjected to rape by the appellant and on the pretext of marriage he continued to establish relationship with her which resulted in her becoming pregnant on three occasions and each time the pregnancy was aborted.
Submission has been advanced by the learned counsel for the appellant that the age of the victim has not been properly assessed.
It has further been submitted that as per the victim who has been examined as P.W. 1, she was in love with the appellant and wanted to solemnize marriage with him.

He further submits that the case was instituted at the behest of the mother of the victim who has been examined as P.W. 2 who has stated in her evidence that she did not want the victim to marry the present appellant and that was the reason, the case was instituted by her.

So far as the allegation Santosh Oraon vs The State Of Jharkhand on 8 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/193762312/
1 of abortion is concerned, reference has been made to the evidence of the doctor who has been examined as P.W. 3 and who has stated in her evidence that there is no medical evidence to corroborate the story of abortion.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned A.P.P. for the State has opposed the prayer for bail of the appellant.
In view of the evidence of P.W. 1 apart from the evidence of mother of the victim, we are inclined to admit the appellant on bail.

Accordingly, during the pendency of this appeal, the appellant above named is directed to be released on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs. 10,000/- (Ten Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each, to the satisfaction of the learned Special Judge (POCSO), Lohardaga in connection with Special POCSO Case No. 28 of 2023.
I. A. No. 5096 of 2025 stands disposed of.
